newsitem.title: USA: "King of Pop" launches new album with low-key approach.
newsitem.headline: "King of Pop" launches new album with low-key approach.

text.p: Michael Jackson is coming out with an album this month but times have changed for the self-proclaimed "King of Pop" and the record industry since his last disc was launched with enormous fanfare.
"In the last decade, the marketing of Jackson's product has always been bombastic," said Thomas White, an artists' rights expert who represents the estates of stars like the late Fred Astaire.

"Usually every available media outlet is saturated with imagery depicting him in the center of legions of followers," he said, referring to the marketing blitz accompanying Jackson's last album "HIStory - Past, Present and Future Book 1," which was released in 1995.

Some record industry sources said Epic Records, a Sony Corp. record label, is taking a more low-key approach in releasing "Blood on the Dance Floor:HIStory in the Mix" May 20 after Jackson's 1995 album fell short of expectations.
Worldwide sales of the 1995 double compact disc have hit 13 million, while Jackson's earlier "Thriller" album has sold 44 million worldwide, an Epic spokesman said.

Others familiar with the situation said the launch has been more subdued because it is a typical approach for releases of re-mix albums. The new album includes only five new songs among its 13 tracks.

Nevertheless, music retailers, which are experiencing a slump, often lament that today's pop artists lack the staying and sales power of Jackson. And they are looking forward to the album's release, regardless of the marketing strategy.

"We know it's coming out and it will be probably do very well," said Fred Durrie, a dance music buyer for Tower Records. "The single 'Blood on the Dance Floor' is selling amazingly well and everything he touches turns to gold."

He said the last album in 1995 was surrounded by so much marketing to deflect media attention over allegations that Jackson sexually molested a young boy. Jackson vehemently denied the charges and Los Angeles prosecutors decided not to file criminal charges in late 1994 after the boy refused to cooperate.
That came after Jackson agreed in January 1994 to pay the boy a multi-million dollar settlement in return for dropping a civil lawsuit against the singer.
"There was so much going on with his life last time," Durrie said.
The pop star's latest album seems to come at a much happier time in his life.

In November 1996, Jackson married Debbie Rowe who recently gave birth to Jackson's son. Rowe was pregnant when the couple was married shortly after the singer divorced Lisa Marie Presley, the daughter of late rock 'n roll legend Elvis Presley, following a 20-month marriage.

Meanwhile, Jackson arrived in Cannes, France, for the film festival last week for the opening of his 38-minute film, "Ghosts", which is the first part of a major attempt by Jackson to re-launch his flagging career.
